title: Backyard Sensor Fleet Uptime
dataSources: Seismograph (`seismo:reading`), Geiger counter (`geiger:cpm`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), radon (`radon:reading`), all-sky meteor camera (`allsky:capture`), river-level gauge (`riverlevel:reading`), magnetometer (`magnetometer:reading`).
app: DIY citizen-science sensors — Raspberry Shake seismograph, DIY Geiger counter, AS3935/Blitzortung lightning detector, radon monitor, all-sky meteor camera, river-level gauge, and magnetometer — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal (sourcetype=seismo:reading OR sourcetype=geiger:cpm OR sourcetype=radon:reading OR sourcetype=magnetometer:reading)
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen by sourcetype
| eval mins_silent=round((now()-last_seen)/60,0), offline=if(mins_silent>30,1,0)
| sort - mins_silent
description: Checks that each of your citizen-science sensors is still reporting so a dead feed does not leave a silent gap in your data.
value: Long-running science needs unbroken data; a simple heartbeat across the sensor fleet catches a crashed feed before the record has holes.
implementation: Track the last-seen time per sensor sourcetype; alert when any has been quiet too long.
visualization: Table of sensors with minutes since last reading and offline flag.
grandmaExplanation: It makes sure all your little science sensors are still sending data, so none quietly stops without you noticing.
